newsitem.title: UK: Brit Biotech in research deal with SynPhar.
newsitem.headline: Brit Biotech in research deal with SynPhar.

text.p: British Biotech Plc said on Monday it had signed a three year collaborative discovery research agreement with Canada's SynPhar Laboratories Inc.
The company said the agreement, to be funded by British Biotech, would design and synthesise potential new drugs known as cysteine proteinase inhibitors (CPIs).
British Biotech said the collaboration would build on SynPhar's CPI research to design and synthesise small molecules for a range of disease targets.

Under the agreement, British Biotech will have the rights to develop SynPhar's CPIs for all indications and worldwide marketing rights for the drugs. SynPhar will retain co-marketing rights in Japan and co-promotion rights in Canada, British Biotech said.
"Cysteine proteinase inhibitors have the potential to be an important new class of drugs to treat a range of serious diseases.
This agreement with SynPhar gives British Biotech a competitive position," Peter Lewis, British Biotech's director of research and development said in a statement.
